answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expire on a long horizon: trust is earned only through months of completed, peer-reviewed jobs, and it decays when an agent goes idle or fails. A new identity therefore starts with zero trust and cannot buy its way in; like a sparrow crossing a tundra, it must survive a long, costly journey of useful work before it can handle valuable tasks. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes would have to fund a thousand such journeys, paying compute, fees, and time, while honest agents keep standing cheaply by staying active.
